question.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨{t}^{2},\,1,\,3t⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,0,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨{t}^{2},\,1,\,3t⟩\cdot ⟨2t,\,0,\,3⟩ \\  & =2{t}^{3}+9t \\  & =t(2{t}^{2}+9), \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{({t}^{2})}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}+{(3t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{4}+9{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{t(2{t}^{2}+9)}{\sqrt{{t}^{4}+9{t}^{2}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$
